description: Verify ARP cache merge on two consecutive gratuitous Responses from the same IP with different MACs — gratuitous variant of ARP_32, requires arp_accept=1
approach:
[Objective]
Gratuitous Response variant of ARP_32. The same merge-overwrite invariant from RFC 826 §2.3 must hold whether the seeding stimulus is a Request (ARP_32) or a gratuitous Response (this case). Linux requires `net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept=1` on DUT for gratuitous announcements to be honoured (set by setup-netns.sh).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response #1 (sender_ip=HOST-1-IP, sender_mac=MAC-ADDR1)

2. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response #2 (sender_ip=HOST-1-IP, sender_mac=MAC-ADDR2)
   ⇒ Cache entry must now hold MAC-ADDR2.

3. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup → DUT sends UDP.

4. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: UDP with eth_dst == MAC-ADDR2   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DUT's UDP eth_dst equals MAC-ADDR2.

[Fail condition]
Same as ARP_32 — Fail_used_mac1 / Fail_unknown_mac / Fail_dut_arp_request / Fail_timeout.

verdicts.Pass: DUT used MAC-ADDR2 — gratuitous merge worked
verdicts.Fail_used_mac1: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 — merge did not overwrite
verdicts.Fail_unknown_mac: DUT used some other MAC — cache corrupt
verdicts.Fail_dut_arp_request: DUT re-resolved via its own Request — cache not populated
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit UDP within window
